add_block.new_heading: Where to get oysters in Dubai — and where to buy them yourself
new_paragraphs: Two different questions hide inside that one. If you want to eat oysters tonight, the hotel seafood restaurants and a handful of dedicated raw bars around the city shuck them by the half-dozen. If you want to buy oysters in Dubai and open them at home, the fish markets are the direct route, and the Waterfront Market in Deira is the largest of them. The seafood counters in the bigger supermarkets also keep oysters chilled on ice next to the prawns and crab. Specialist seafood importers also deliver, and they are the better call when you need a particular variety or a count above a dozen or two, because a market counter sells whatever landed that morning.

Whichever route you take, check the same things before you pay. Shells should be shut tight. Tap one that is gaping and it should close; if it stays open the oyster is dead, so leave it. They should feel heavy for their size, sit cup-down on ice instead of swimming in meltwater, and carry a harvest or packing date on the box. Ask the counter for the variety name and where it was farmed. Anyone selling good oysters knows both, and the answer also tells you how long they have been out of the water.

Shucking four dozen an hour before guests arrive is slow, awkward work, and unkind to your hands without the right knife and glove. That is what the catering side of this page is for. Partners buy through Dubai seafood suppliers, not retail counters, keep everything chilled and unopened until it is opened in front of guests, and put the varieties and their origin on your proposal so you know what is arriving.

add_block.new_heading: The raw bar menu in full — course by course
new_paragraphs: Here is the repertoire we build from, in the order it reaches a guest. Almost nobody takes all of it. A cocktail reception might use the first four sections and stop; a seated dinner draws one dish from each and runs them as courses. Tell us which sections you want and the proposal comes back with those lines and no others. One honest caveat first: species and varieties move with the season, with what is landing, and with the quality of the goods that arrive on the day. Anyone who promises you a fixed list twelve months out has not bought fish in July.
1. The raw bar — oysters and shellfish on ice

This is the centrepiece and the section worth reading closely, because named provenance is the clearest divide between a real raw bar and a tray of chilled shellfish. The varieties that turn up on serious Dubai raw bars are Dibba Bay , farmed in UAE waters and the only local one of the group, then Gillardeau , Tarbouriech and Fine de Claire from France, and Kelly native Irish . We quote by variety and by the farm the batch came from instead of writing the word "oysters" and leaving you to guess, and the varieties confirmed for your date are printed on the proposal.
Shucked-to-order oyster selection — two to four named varieties on crushed ice, opened in front of guests, served cup-down with the liquor intact.
Composed seafood platter — crayfish, langoustine, mud crab, mussels, scallops, tiger prawns, smoked salmon and cured tuna, built on a tiered ice display.
Per-person shellfish plate — six oysters, six prawns, half a lobster and tourteau crab rillettes, with shallot vinegar, lemon and hand-made mayonnaise.
Colossal shrimp cocktail , served in the glass with cocktail sauce and tabasco.
Edible oyster shell, yuzu fizz and chilli — the flavour of the raw bar for guests who will not eat the texture.
Caviar éclair , and an Ossetra caviar service in 30g, 50g, 125g and 250g tins, spooned tableside from mother-of-pearl. It sits on the quote as its own line, because it should be yours to take off.
2. Crudo — cured, tartare and ceviche
Where a raw bar shows whether it can cook. All of it is prepared cold and plated to order, and every marinade here is written alcohol-free by default.
Sea bass ceviche, kumquat, yellow chilli, passion fruit, herb oil, avocado, purple corn crackers
Salmon tartare, lemon crème fraîche, chives, caviar, in a fennel-scented cone
Cured vanilla tuna, pickled apple, fennel flower salad, preserved lemon curd
Smoked salmon, beetroot relish, brandy snap, mustard cress
Scallop sashimi, yuzu, air-dried ginger, asparagus and shiso
Trio of tartare — tuna, salmon and beef, served together on one board
Cured salmon, hamachi sashimi, caramelised o’toro and kingfish, cut as a tasting flight
Tuna ceviche with jalapeño, for the taco station
3. The sushi and sashimi counter

A separate live counter with its own chefs, cutting to order, not plating trays made an hour earlier. The benchmark spread on the strongest Dubai menus is ten maki, four sashimi or nigiri and four uramaki, and that is what we quote unless you want it narrower.
Maki: beef tataki · tempura prawn · pickled Japanese vegetable · California roll · salmon avocado · tempura soft-shell crab · prawn wakame · marinated BBQ eel · confit duck foie gras · spicy tuna
Sashimi and nigiri: kingfish · salmon · seabass · prawn
Uramaki: tuna · scallop · wagyu · duck
Without seafood: vegetable maki and the pickled Japanese vegetable roll, cut on the same counter so vegetarian guests queue at the same counter as the rest of the room, not at a side table.
4. Passed seafood canapés and hot bites
The section that lets the raw bar travel around the room instead of holding guests in one corner. Most items can be made in a smaller size for a standing reception.
Squid “risotto”, prawn broth, black coral wafer
Smoked eel and beetroot relish beignet, preserved lemon fluid gel
Za’atar loukoumades, taramosalata, salmon caviar, preserved lemon
Smoked scallop mousseline, snow crab, caviar and gold leaf, as a one-bite sandwich
Prawn “popcorn” dynamite, lime aioli, pickled ginger, seaweed cone, popping candy
Seared scallop taco, duck prosciutto, pine nut and raisin salsa
Salmon fish cakes · fried cod · crab bonda · prawn laksa
Crab cakes · bang bang prawns · prawn and coriander fritters · gratinated herb mussels · smoked salmon pâté
Crab-stuffed mushrooms, the one canapé that survives a boat deck without wilting
5. Live stations — robata, grill, hot pot and the trolley

Hot seafood cooked in front of guests, which is what stops a raw bar feeling like a cold buffet halfway through the evening. Each station is quoted separately because each one needs its own equipment and its own chefs on it.

Where each hot station can stand is a venue question rather than a menu one, and it is worth settling before the menu is signed. The robata counter burns live charcoal, so it runs outdoors on a villa plot — Dubai Municipality’s barbecue guidance is explicit that coal is never lit indoors or in an enclosed space — while on a beach it needs either a permitted private event or the beach club’s own sign-off, because lighting a fire outside a designated zone on an open public beach is a Dubai Municipality offence carrying a Dh500 fine. For a rooftop or a desert camp, myCHEF confirms the charcoal position with the building management or the site operator before quoting rather than assuming it. On a yacht the robata is out: no additional gas or fuel cylinder may be brought aboard (D-Marin Art. 53.1(a)) and Dubai Harbour bans the operation of gas cylinders on marina premises, so charter crews run the boat’s own fitted grill while the chef preps, plates and serves. An apartment is closed to it as well, since Emaar’s vertical-community rules prohibit barbecues, grills or cooking equipment of any kind on balconies and terraces whatever the fuel. In both of those settings the same skewers run on an electric or induction yakitori counter, or are charred over charcoal in the licensed partner kitchen and finished in front of guests at the counter. The smokehouse follows the same logic: a live smoker is a solid-fuel appliance with a long burn, so it belongs on an open private plot and is confirmed per booking anywhere else, and where it cannot run the salmon and ocean trout are smoked in the licensed kitchen, held, and sliced to order on the station — which is how smoked fish reaches most events anyway. The raw bar itself carries no heat source at all, and that is why it travels everywhere in the city: villa, beach, rooftop, apartment, desert camp or yacht deck, with nothing to plan beyond ice, drainage and shade.
Robata grill: tsukune shrimp balls, scallop, shrimp and salmon, handed over the counter straight off the charcoal.
Live seafood grill: prawns, octopus and giant squid, marinated and turned to order.
Interactive hot pot: halibut and prawn cooked in miso, gochujang, star anise chicken or mushroom dashi broths, with fried silken tofu and vegetables for guests eating no seafood.
Carving station: salt-crusted whole salmon, cracked open and carved in front of the room.
Smokehouse: smoked salmon and smoked ocean trout, sliced to order.
Market-style seafood counter: the day’s catch laid out on ice and cooked to order, guest by guest.
Oyster trolley: the shucking moves through the room instead of standing still, which works far better at a wedding where nobody wants to leave their table.
6. Seafood mains, plated or on the buffet
Two to four of these on a buffet, or two or three fish and shellfish courses inside a plated menu.
Halibut, celeriac purée, green beans, pumpkin, pickled radish and dill
Salmon, fennel, cauliflower purée, green beans, carrots, spinach, gremolata
Miso and honey glazed salmon fillet
Chermoula-marinated cod
Jumbo prawns · Hokkaido scallop · wild seabass · blue swimmer crab · langoustine
Red chilli prawns — Gulf prawns pan-fried with garlic, ginger, red chilli, lemongrass and cream, with jasmine rice
Lobster roll, warm butter, in a toasted split bun
7. Seafood salads and cold sides
Tuna niçoise — heirloom tomatoes, olives, chat potatoes, white anchovies, mustard vinaigrette
Prawn and wakame salad
Grilled calamari salad
8. Daytime, boardroom and drop-off seafood
The same repertoire re-cut for a working lunch or a boardroom, where there is no station and no service team, only good food arriving on time.
House-smoked BBQ salmon, pickled fennel, pickled beetroot, avocado, roquette, dill Japanese mayonnaise
Vietnamese banh mi, tempura cod, pickled carrot, cucumber, mint, coriander, Thai mayonnaise
Rare tuna, pickled fennel, remoulade salad, gherkins, dill mayonnaise
Vitello tonnato — shaved veal, tuna yuzu mayonnaise, capers, anchovies, roquette
Crab, salmon and caviar crumpet · ocean trout crêpes in brioche
Smoked salmon, pickled cucumber, red onion and mayonnaise
9. Sauces, condiments and the presentation kit

Weak menus leave this section out entirely and write “served with sauces&rdquo. Here is the whole tray, named: shallot vinegar mignonette, lemon wedges, hand-made mayonnaise, lime aioli, cocktail sauce, tabasco, ponzu, yuzu, soy, wasabi and pickled ginger, with garlic butter and spicy marinades for the grill. The display itself is part of the deliverable, not an afterthought: a drained crushed-ice bed, a tiered ice tower, and seaweed and citrus dressing the shells. Every mignonette, marinade and finishing sauce is written alcohol-free as standard, and halal sourcing is confirmed in writing before the menu is signed off.
10. Dessert

No seafood category has its own desserts, so this comes from the wider menu: a dessert and crêpe station, a sweet ending station of small pastries and fruit, or a plated final course if the evening is seated.
Vegetarian, vegan and dietary requirements alongside the raw bar

In this category a vegetarian answer means a parallel offering, not a modified dish, so we build one: vegetable maki and the pickled Japanese vegetable roll on the sushi counter, fried silken tofu and vegetables in the hot pot, and a separate non-seafood station where the guest numbers justify it. Shellfish is one of the most common serious allergies there is, which makes this the section to raise early, not on the night.

Gluten-free, nut-conscious and other dietary menu options may be available on request, subject to confirmation by the assigned culinary partner. Partner kitchens may handle allergens, and cross-contact cannot be completely excluded unless dedicated controls have been specifically confirmed for the booking. Guests with allergies must provide full details before confirming their event.

add_block.new_heading: How much does oyster bar catering cost in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: A staffed raw bar starts from AED 700–950 per person, with the final oyster bar catering cost set by guest count, the varieties you choose and the service level. Per-head pricing suits most receptions; larger celebrations often move to package pricing, and our chef-led experience packages run at AED 1,200, 2,400, 3,600, 4,500 and 5,500 depending on scope, with a dedicated tasting menu available at AED 1,400. Premium species, live lobster and add-on seafood push the number up, so a pared-back station and a full manned luxury display are genuinely different products at genuinely different prices. For a clear breakdown, see our prices page and the catering price guide , or send your details for an itemised quote and you'll get real figures, not a vague range.
Is there such a thing as cheap oyster bar catering in Dubai?

Cheap is the wrong word for a raw bar, and we would sooner say so than pretend otherwise. Oysters are imported, perishable and opened one at a time by hand, and none of that gets less expensive by wanting it to. What you can control is scope, and three levers do the work. Cut the count per guest to 4–6 as a reception centrepiece instead of 8–12 as the main event. Shorten the service window, since a station open for an hour costs less to staff than one open for three. Or drop the manned station altogether and take the same seafood as part of a chilled canapé or buffet menu, which starts from AED 150 per person instead of AED 700. That last one is the honest budget answer: the same prawns, crab and smoked salmon on the table, no shucker on the floor.
Are there oyster bar catering Dubai offers or seasonal deals?

No discount codes, no seasonal offers, no book-by-Friday pricing. We don't run them, because a rate that only exists during a promotion was not the real rate. What we publish instead are the numbers themselves: from AED 700–950 per person for the staffed raw bar, from AED 150 per person on a canapé or buffet menu, and fixed chef-led packages at AED 1,200, 2,400, 3,600, 4,500 and 5,500. Scope is the only thing that moves your total, and every part of it (oyster count, service hours, staff, add-on seafood) shows up as its own line on the proposal, so you can take a line out and see the price change instead of haggling over a bundle.
Is there a minimum number of guests or a minimum spend?

The staffed raw bar is priced per head, so there is no fixed minimum headcount, and a raw bar for a small dinner party at home is a real booking, not a favour. A minimum order value of AED 900 applies across myCHEF, and the buffet and canapé formats start at 20 guests. That sits in line with the Dubai market: Elements asks for 20 on buffets, Al Safadi for 30 on every buffet package, and Taste Studio takes business-lunch delivery from 10 people.

add_block.new_heading: What is the leading catering company in Dubai?
new_paragraphs: There isn't one, and a company that says it is has told you about its copywriter, not its kitchen. The names that come up most often across the searches we tracked are Cedar Tree Catering, Elements Catering, Taste Studio and Al Safadi. All four are real and established, and each is stronger at a different job. Elements publishes detailed per-head menus for buffets, live stations and plated dinners. Al Safadi is the Levantine buffet specialist and asks for 30 people on every package. Taste Studio is built around corporate lunch delivery. Cedar Tree covers the widest ground of the four.

So judge on what you can check instead of on the adjective. Does the company publish a price for its own work, or only "request a quote"? Two of the biggest names in Dubai catering publish no prices at all, and one of them ranks a blog about what catering costs in the city while quoting no rate of its own. Does it state a minimum headcount and a lead time before you call? Will it name the chef who turns up? Can it tell you where the food came from? Those four answers separate caterers faster than any ranking does.

On oysters specifically the field narrows, because a manned raw bar is a different job from putting chilled prawns on a platter. It needs a trained shucker, a cold chain that holds in Dubai heat, and a station that still looks good at hour three. It is fair to ask any caterer, us included, how many they have run and what the plan is if the ice starts losing the fight. We publish our rate, our minimum and our timings on this page for exactly that reason.

add_block.new_heading: Oyster bar catering — frequently asked questions
new_paragraphs: How much does oyster bar catering cost in Dubai?

A staffed raw bar with a shucker on station runs from AED 700–950 per person, quoted by group size, oyster variety and service level. On a chilled canapé or buffet menu with no station, the same seafood starts from AED 150 per person. Send your details for an exact quote and you'll get real figures within one business day.
Where can I buy oysters in Dubai?

For buying them yourself, the fish markets are the direct route — the Waterfront Market in Deira is the largest — and the seafood counters in the bigger supermarkets keep them chilled on ice. Specialist seafood importers deliver and are the better option for a particular variety or a large count. Check the shells are shut tight, heavy for their size and sitting cup-down on ice, and ask for the variety name and the farm it came from.
How do you eat oysters at an oyster bar?

Check it looks plump and sits in clear liquor, run the small fork underneath to be sure the muscle is cut, and taste the first one undressed before adding lemon or mignonette. Bring the wide end of the shell to your lips, tip the oyster and its liquor in together, and chew two or three times instead of swallowing it whole. Work from the smaller, milder oysters to the larger, brinier ones, and put the empty shells back on the ice upside down.
How many oysters should I plan per guest?
Plan 4–6 oysters per guest when the raw bar is a reception centrepiece, or 8–12 when it's the main event. Your caterer confirms counts once the guest list and format are set.
Where do the oysters come from and are they fresh?

Partners buy through Dubai seafood suppliers, not retail counters, and they stay chilled and unopened until they are shucked in front of guests, so nothing sits pre-opened. We don't name one supplier here because supply follows what lands fresh, but the varieties and where they were farmed go on your proposal. The chefs we work with operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements throughout.
Is there such a thing as cheap oyster bar catering in Dubai?

No. Oysters are imported, perishable and opened by hand. What lowers the bill honestly is fewer oysters per guest, a shorter service window, or moving the seafood onto a chilled canapé or buffet menu from AED 150 per person instead of a staffed station at AED 700.
Are there oyster bar catering Dubai offers or seasonal deals?
No discount codes and no seasonal offers. We publish the rate itself instead, and every element of scope appears as its own line on the proposal so you can see what removing it saves.
Is there a minimum number of guests or a minimum spend?
No fixed minimum headcount for the staffed raw bar, since it's priced per head. A minimum order value of AED 900 applies across myCHEF, and the buffet and canapé formats start at 20 guests.
Can you cater a corporate oyster bar or a private party?
Yes. We arrange corporate oyster bar catering for launches and galas and oyster bar party catering for weddings, yachts and villa celebrations, scaled from intimate gatherings to large receptions.
What's included in the oyster bar service?
Included are menu design, a vetted chef or shucker, the seafood, the ice display, accompaniments, on-site service and setup, and cleanup where relevant — a full-service raw bar, not a drop-off.
Do you offer non-alcoholic pairings and other seafood?
Yes. Alongside oysters we serve a chilled seafood selection and mocktail or citrus pairings, so guests who don't eat raw oysters still enjoy a full spread.
How do I book an oyster bar in Dubai?
Booking is clear: tell us your date, guest count and venue, we send an itemised proposal, then match a vetted chef to your event. Most proposals go out within one business day.
For oyster bar catering, the chefs and partner kitchens handling your booking operate to Dubai Municipality food-safety requirements .

new_paragraphs: Send your date, guest count and venue, and your proposal arrives.
Book with 3–5 days notice for a live shucking station or any multi-staff event, and 7–14 days for weddings, corporate functions and larger productions. Those are preferred lead times, not a cut-off.
Confirm the menu and the oyster count about 7 days out, when the guest list is firm.
Ask early about allergies and shellfish-free plates, not in the last 48 hours .
Check the access route and where the ice can drain, because setup starts roughly 2 hours ahead.
Plan on roughly 3 hours of service, and add 5% VAT to the total.

We recommend booking as early as possible. Lead times depend on guest numbers, menu complexity, staffing, equipment, location and partner availability. A oyster bar at short notice is sometimes workable - availability is confirmed individually, never assumed.
Get a proposal or ask on WhatsApp .
